## Contract review brief — PR #37043 @ `63287424a22bff43b285da9d0b731e506c965d25` (card #36630)

You review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Render ONE `## Contract review` record on this head — its shape is
`node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template` — with a PASS or FAIL verdict, and post it as ONE comment
on the PR or its card.

Inputs — these and nothing else:
  · card #36630: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
  · PR #37043: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `63287424a22bff43b285da9d0b731e506c965d25`
  · the check-runs on `63287424a22bff43b285da9d0b731e506c965d25`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts
⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.

Scope — the paths `reviewFace` returns as `hits` on this PR's file list: skills/objectstack-ui/rules/actions.md, skills/objectstack-ui/evals/views-apps-actions-pages.json;
  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
  a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
  ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

Security — if a `hits` path is under `skills/**` or `ui/skills/**` and the change teaches security, auth or permission
  behaviour the path name doesn't show, the record says so and the seat adopting the record adds the `security` label.
  The record says so on its `Security-touching:` line, and the arm lands on `no` alone: write `no` ONLY when no changed
  hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token, authentication or other security behaviour, else `yes`.

Rule change — if a `hits` path is under `.claude/**`: the PR body declares `Rule-change:` and you verify it against the diff.
  Write `Rule-change-verified: none` ONLY when no changed hunk alters what an agent may do without the maintainer
  (merge, bypass a check, change repository settings), what gets done and in what order (grading, dispatch, scope), or
  what must go to him (decisions, maintainer actions); process steps, scripts, wording, slimming and file moves are not rule
  changes. Write `ruled` ONLY when every such hunk copies the ruling the PR body quotes on its `Ruling-ref:` line — check the
  copy against the quoted words, do not re-rule it. Otherwise `yes`: the pull request then waits for the maintainer.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-objectstack/177ababb-cccd-573a-a846-cda17d8e5bbd/scratchpad/pr-37043/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST
thing after each colon.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `63287424a22bff43b285da9d0b731e506c965d25`
Local-runs: probe — byte count of the post-image of rules/actions.md rebuilt from the diff, to check the ceiling is pinned at the measurement; no gate, build or test was run
Scope: skills/objectstack-ui/rules/actions.md, skills/objectstack-ui/evals/views-apps-actions-pages.json + scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: none

Read for this record: card #36630 (body and its 4 comments: triage 7091886018, claim 7138343252, dev reports 7138721425 and 7138853384), PR #37043 (body, 4 files, net diff), the 49 check-runs on the head, and the cited code on `main` at `b01d8f97`.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set: no change. The diff touches no schema, validator or runtime code. Right.
- Published surface (`@objectstack/skills`): `rules/actions.md` gains one section of 9 body lines, "Button Order (`actionLayout`)", and loses one parenthetical example; 14842 to 15519 bytes. Right: it is the teaching the card orders, and it agrees with the merged code (④).
- Eval fixture: case 24 appended after case 23 (ids on `main` run 1 to 23). Measured, not ratcheted, inert in a consumer install. Right.
- Gate constant: the `CEILINGS` row for `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/actions.md` moves 3711 to 3880. Right under the script header's raise rule (③).
- Check-runs on the head: every one is `success` or `skipped`, none red and none pending at the time of reading. `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `TypeScript Type Check` and `Test Core` all read `success`. These are the gate verdicts; nothing was re-run.

### ② Semver level

`patch` for `@objectstack/skills` is the right level: the diff publishes teaching text for a key that already ships, plus one eval case; nothing new is accepted or refused, and `scripts/` is not published. The `Clause-②: no` line on the PR body and in the changeset holds: no narrowing and no accept-set change. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds. The changeset's summary sentence matches the section as it stands on this head (it no longer claims the shape refusals the fix round cut).

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags, first report (7138721425):
- Changeset file outside the claimed surface: accepted. The package is published, the file is new, `Check Changeset` is green.
- Ratchet left red, and the one `open_questions` entry (how the +233 overrun is paid): answered by the fix round, judged below. Closed.
- Local gate set narrowed, `check:skill-examples` not measured locally: answered by the head's check-runs, all green; the diff adds no marked example block.
- Commit trailer in the repo's model-free pair: that is the AGENTS.md rule; nothing to answer on a reviewed face.

Dev flags, second report (7138853384), `open_questions` empty:
- PR body left for the seat: the body as read carries the fix round's readings (head `63287424a2`, 15519 bytes, 3880 tokens) and quotes the ruling. Closed.
- Only one same-file restatement found: judged below; my own read of the file found no second one.
- The section no longer spells the shape refusals (a fourth pin, a name twice) nor the default-order sentence: accepted. "at most 3" stays, the schema's own refusal messages name the fix, and "every other action goes to the ⋯ menu, those `more` names first" keeps the order of unnamed actions.
- File surface widened to the ratchet row by the seat: the row is reviewed here as the implementing file.
- Out-of-scope note, the evals README summary does not mention the button-order case: accepted as a deviation. The summary is a descriptive list and no gate reads it.
- `security_findings: none`: agreed. The one sentence weighed for the security line is the `.custom` writer rule. It teaches which package's extension may write an arrangement key (ADR-0146 D10, judged on package identity, the rule objectstack-data already teaches for `fieldGroups`); it teaches no permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication behaviour. The eval's `share` is an action name only.

The ratchet row against the script header's raise rule (standing ruling, record 6513306068):
1. Deletion of restatement in the same file, shown in the diff: yes. The copy-holes bullet loses the 49-byte parenthetical example beside `description`. It restated: the rule sentence stays whole, the hole spelling is still shown by the `helpText` bullet below it and by the Reassign Lead block's `successMessage`, and no eval token rests on the removed words.
2. The PR body quotes the ruling: yes, the 2026-10-27 words and the record number.
3. The measured remainder, pinned at the measurement: the pre-image blob `c662acc6` is the file on `main`, 14842 bytes, 3711 tokens, zero headroom. The section adds 726 bytes, the cut removes 49, the post-image is 15519 bytes and its blob id equals the head's (`2652f16d`). ceil(15519 / 4) is 3880, the row is 3880, headroom 0, +169.
4. The row's note: same form as the row's earlier notes, and each of its sentences checks against the diff (the placement, the content list, the cut's exact bytes, the arithmetic, the ruling quote, the audit formula).
5. The 10402 principle: one new authorable key, teaching the card orders, cut from +233 to +169 before the raise. In proportion with the row's earlier entries.
The raise holds.

SQL push-down: not applicable. No query, no id materialisation and no join in the diff.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

`skills/objectstack-ui/rules/actions.md`, sentence by sentence against `main`:
- Shape and limit: `pinned` is required, takes at most 3 entries, `[]` pins none, `more` is optional; unpinned actions go to the overflow, the ones `more` names first (`packages/spec/src/data/object-action-layout.ts`, `arrangedHeaderActions` in `ui/packages/types/src/ui-action.ts`). Holds.
- The inline example names `crm_convert_lead` and `crm_print_a3`, both declared in the same file on `lead` at `record_header`, so it passes the reference rule it sits beside. Holds.
- `record` takes `record_header` / `record_more`, `list` takes `list_toolbar` (`ARM_LOCATIONS` in `packages/lint/src/validate-object-action-layout.ts`). Record page, side preview and phone bar read one arranged list (`RecordDetailView.tsx`; an authored `page:header` with `placedActions: true` reads the same). Holds.
- `$import` / `$export` are the list scope's built-ins and pinned only (`OBJECT_ACTION_LAYOUT_BUILTINS`, `moreEntryRefusal`). Holds.
- `os validate` refuses a name the scope does not place: `validateObjectActionLayout` is a gating rule on validate, build and lint, with `object-action-layout-unknown` and `object-action-layout-not-placed` at error. Holds for the object's own key, the position the paragraph is written about.
- The `.custom` writer and "each arm whole": `CUSTOM_ARRANGEMENT_KEYS` and the `ObjectExtensionSchema.actionLayout` description. The pointer "(as `fieldGroups`, objectstack-data)" lands on a sentence that exists and teaches that writer rule and its doors. Holds.
- Reachable: the "Where to go" row of `SKILL.md` ("A button or operation") routes to this file, and no sibling rule file teaches a competing header order.

- N1 (nit) — "wherever that header draws (record page, side preview, phone bar, a row's ⋮ menu order)" lists the row menu among the places the header draws. The header does not draw there: a row's menu lists its own actions and takes the arm's ORDER for the ones the arm names (`rowActionArrangement.ts`). The word "order" carries the true reading and the `locations` table right above keeps `list_item` as the row placement, so no wrong metadata follows.
- N2 (nit) — "`os validate` refuses a name the arm's scope does not place" is unqualified, and the next sentence teaches the `.custom` extension. The validator judges an extension only against an object the same stack defines; a pair's extension of an installed object is skipped (its test: "skips one whose object the stack does not define"), so there a wrong name draws nothing and `os validate` says nothing. The sentence is true where it is written; a reader who carries it onto the next sentence over-reads it. The placement rule itself is taught correctly, so the author still names the right actions.

`skills/objectstack-ui/evals/views-apps-actions-pages.json`, case 24, against the card's ask and the section:
- The prompt asks for four header buttons, so the limit is what is exercised; the expected output (three pinned, Share leading `more`, `$export` pinned in the `list` arm after `mass_assign`, no `order` renumbering, no page file) follows from the section alone and agrees with the schema: a fourth pin is refused, `$export` in `more` is refused, a name not placed at `list_toolbar` is refused by `os validate`, and `order` is shared by every surface. Every `must_contain` token is in this bundle. Holds.
- The card's four teaching items (key shape, the pinned limit, what each arm reaches, the `.custom` arrangement) are all in the section; the case exercises the first two and the list built-in. The `.custom` rule is taught by pointer into another bundle, so leaving it ungraded here is sound.
- N3 (nit) — the assertions are loose in both directions: `'clone', 'share']` catches a four-name `pinned` only in single quotes with that spacing, and it and `definePage` would also reject a correct answer that quotes the refused form. This is the fixture's existing practice (case 23 beside it); the grader's `expected_output` carries the real judgment.

`scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`: one row and its note. The number and every sentence of the note agree with the diff and with the raise rule (③). No other line of the script moves.

The three nits need no move of this head; each is the seat's to leave as an accepted deviation or to card. Read, not reviewed: the sentence in `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md` that the new pointer lands on names `fieldGroups` and `relatedLists` only, two of the three keys `CUSTOM_ARRANGEMENT_KEYS` now holds. That file is outside this diff and the card's surface.

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：用户无感。AI 写应用时会用对象的 `actionLayout` 排列记录页和列表页上的按钮（最多固定 3 个，其余进「更多」），而不是去改每个动作的序号或写页面文件。
- 为什么做：这个能力已上线，但技能文档没教，AI 只能猜。
- 出错会怎样：只是教学文字和一道评测题；最坏是 AI 写出的按钮顺序不对，`os validate` 会拒收写错的名字。
- 要你做什么：批准合并。因为同时把技能字数上限脚本里的一个数从 3711 调到 3880（同文件先删 49 字节，再按实测抬高，引常设裁决 6513306068），所以要人工批准。契约审核 PASS：记录 7139491356，Head-sha `63287424a22bff43b285da9d0b731e506c965d25`。

席位意见：可以合并。文字逐句与已上线行为一致；上限只抬到实测值，没有余量。
